content.title: Scottie Scheffler | Major Wins, Age, Wife, & Career
content.text: Top Questions What were Scottie Scheffler’s major achievements in 2024? When did Scottie Scheffler first become ranked number one in golf? Which major tournaments has Scottie Scheffler won? News • Scottie Scheffler (born June 21, 1996, Ridgewood, New Jersey, U.S.) is an American golfer who in 2024 had the best single-season performance by a pro since the heyday of Tiger Woods. That year Scheffler played in 19 events and won 7, the biggest one-year total since Woods captured 7 titles in 2007. Among Scheffler’s notable 2024 achievements were winning a second Masters Tournament, earning a gold medal at the Paris Olympic Games, and being named the PGA Tour Player of the Year for the third consecutive year. In 2025 he became only the third golfer in the modern era, after Woods and Jack Nicklaus, to win at least 15 titles, including 3 majors, before age 29. Since notching his first PGA Tour win in 2022, four years after turning pro, Scheffler has distinguished himself as the most consistent player of his generation, which includes compatriots such as Jordan Spieth and Justin Thomas, who had early successes followed by abrupt reversals of fortune. He excels at driving and iron play and has rapidly improved his putting, one of the only discernible weaknesses in his early career. Career highlights Scheffler and his fansScottie Scheffler hitting his second shot on the second hole during the final round of the PGA Championship at Quail Hollow Club on May 18, 2025, in Charlotte, North Carolina. Scheffler won the tournament, earning his first Wanamaker Trophy and third major title.Here are some of Scheffler’s notable achievements in golf. In 2006, the year he turned 10 years old, Scheffler won 19 of the 34 events he entered on the Northern Texas PGA Junior Tour and was named Player of the Year in the boys 12–13 division. Scheffler attended Highland Park High School in Dallas and played on the basketball and golf teams. He won three individual state championships in golf (2012–14). British Open: 2025 2018–19: Scheffler played his first PGA Tour event as a professional in 2018 but spent most of 2018–19 competing on the Korn Ferry Tour, the circuit just below the main tour. In 2019 he entered 20 Korn Ferry Tour tournaments, finishing in the top 10 in half of them and winning two, and was named Korn Ferry Tour Player of the Year.2019–20: He made his first real splash on the PGA Tour in 2020, when he tied for fourth place at the PGA Championship. He was later named PGA Rookie of the Year, having logged six top-five finishes in the 2019–20 season.2020–21: Scheffler entered 29 PGA Tour events and had eight top-10 finishes.2021–22: In February 2022 Scheffler broke through to win his first tournament, at the WM Phoenix Open. He ended up with four victories in the 2021–22 season, including his first major win, at the Masters Tournament. In March 2022 Scheffler was ranked number one for the first time.2022–23: Scheffler continued to have impressive results in the 2022–23 season, notching two wins and 17 top-10 finishes in the 23 events he entered. However, his putting was an obvious weakness, so he hired a putting coach and switched putters toward the beginning of the 2024 season.2024: Scheffler’s banner 2024 season featured seven PGA Tour victories, including his second win at the Masters, and a gold medal at the Paris Olympic Games.2025: In April 2025 Scheffler reached 100 consecutive weeks as the number-one ranked player, having reattained the spot in May 2023. He is the second golfer, after Tiger Woods (who did it twice), to have such a stretch of sustained dominance in golf’s official rankings. Scheffler racked up six tour victories in 2025, including wins at the PGA Championship and the British Open. In addition, he was named the PGA Tour Player of the Year for the fourth consecutive season, matching another feat last achieved by Woods (from 1999 to 2003).2026: Scheffler began the 2026 season with a win in January at the American Express tournament, his 20th PGA Tour victory. He followed that with some uncharacteristically disappointing performances, including two finishes out of the top 20. What’s made Scheffler who he is? Upbringing Scheffler’s remarkable consistency on the PGA Tour is a reflection of the steadiness of his path to becoming a pro. He began playing with a plastic golf club as a toddler in New Jersey. By the time he and his family moved to Dallas in 2002, when he was six years old, he showed enough promise in the sport that his parents took out a loan to join the Royal Oaks Country Club and enlist Randy Smith, a veteran instructor, to coach him. Thereafter Scheffler spent much of his free time at the club, avidly watching older golfers—several of whom were pros—and honing his skills. Scheffler is still an active member at Royal Oaks and, more than two decades later, still employs Smith as his coach. Family and faith Scheffler enjoyed a stable family life. His mother worked as a business executive, and his father stayed at home to raise Scheffler and his three sisters. Scheffler and his wife, Meredith Scheffler (née Scudder), began dating in high school. They married in 2020 and had two sons (born 2024 and 2026). He has frequently spoken about the importance of his Christian faith, which he credits with instilling in him a sense of perspective to counterbalance the ambition of an athletic career. Quick Facts In full: Scott Alexander Scheffler Why was Scheffler arrested in 2024? Because of his relatively low-key public profile, it was especially surprising when Scheffler had a brush with the law in 2024. On May 17 Scheffler was driving early in the morning to play in the second round of the PGA Championship in Louisville, Kentucky. Police were directing traffic around the scene of an earlier accident, and Scheffler was arrested after an officer accused him of failing to follow orders and dragging the officer, who had been holding onto Scheffler’s moving vehicle, for a short distance. The golfer was taken to jail and charged with a felony and several misdemeanors, though the charges were later dropped. Scheffler expressed regret over what he described as “a severe miscommunication in a chaotic situation.”
